answer: An attacker farms masks because one script can speak for all of them. Break that amortization: derive each identity's epoch job from its own key — a distinct slice of ledger history to re-verify and compress into a checksum chain, useful work the network needs. No haven exists for copied summaries, since slices never overlap; like tracing one copper vein through rock, each chain either matches its segment or fails spot re-execution. A juniper planted once still needs its own seasons — likewise every mask must redo the full labor itself, so a thousand masks cost a thousand workloads, not one.
